title: Labs choose, knowledge reward off: α 1, 0.8, 0.2 × 10 runs, $0.15 a lab (Nov 9)

design.question: For the same agents, checker and money, does a community prove more targets when value flows back (OSO) than when results are only shared, or kept private until a target is proved?
design.compare: Labs choose, reward off, α 1, Labs choose, reward off, α 0.8, Labs choose, reward off, α 0.2
design.fixed: the same 4 agents (the single agent: the first, with all the money), $0.60 in all, Lean checks every proof
design.measure: targets proved by the end of a run, of 8; money to reach 2 targets is shown beside it

answer: Most targets proved: Labs choose, reward off, α 0.2, 4.80 of 8.

caveats: Labs could not stop early: each worked until its money or the rounds ran out, so setups are compared at the same money spent.

Rewards differ from the current simulation model: the knowledge reward is off (the simulation pays 1 per new bit since v5): Lean has no agreed measure of a result's new knowledge yet, see docs/design.md; value flowing back is split by the lines each parent saves (its own proof's length in symbols), a stand-in for the work it saves (1/p) in the simulation.
Table values are mean ± standard deviation over runs. Above: means with 95% ranges (Student t), and differences between setups with their 95% ranges; runs are not paired.
